text:
anya: Thinking we should lock down span names + semantic attributes for LLM requests before the next Dedicated rollout. Too many ad-hoc spans in traces right now.

sam: +1. My vote: low-cardinality span names and push detail into attributes. e.g. use `llm.request` and `llm.operation` instead of `gpt4.generate` in the name.

liam: Agree on low-cardinality names. Also: be careful about model versions as raw strings — that can explode cardinality if we attach build IDs. Suggest `llm.model.family` + `llm.model.tag` (stable tag like "v1", "v2-quant") instead.

katie: Can we define a minimal required set? For dashboards we need: model family, operation (generate/embed/rerank), latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_hit bool. Everything else opt-in.

sam: Draft attrs I keep using:
```
span.name = "llm.request"
attributes:
  service.name = "redwood-inference"
  deployment.environment = "prod|staging"
  llm.operation = "generate|embed|rerank|tokenize"
  llm.model.family = "guanaco|redwood-instruct|mistral"
  llm.model.tag = "v1|v2-q8|baseline"
  llm.tokens.input = <int>
  llm.tokens.output = <int>
  llm.cache.hit = true|false
  llm.cache.strategy = "prefix|kv|none"
  tracing.route = "hosted|dedicated|private"
```

liam: Looks good. Two follow-ups: 1) where do we record partial streaming events (token-by-token)? 2) retention concerns — we shouldn't keep token-level events for 90d.

anya: For streaming I'd rather emit lightweight events on span (e.g. span.add_event("tokens_emitted", {"count": 32})) rather than making a new span per chunk. That keeps trace topology sane.

katie: Retention: ops wants 30d for full traces, 90d for error-sampled traces only. Metric backfill for tokens/cost should be longer. So count tokens as metrics (sum per model/route) and avoid storing raw counts in long-lived high-card attrs.

sam: Important note: DO NOT put prompt text or user content in attributes. Hash prompt ids if we need linking: `llm.prompt_id = sha256(id)` or `llm.prompt_hash` and store plain prompt only in opt-in logs for support.

liam: Exporters — we currently ship OTLP to observability-lake and datadog. Need to decide canonical attribute names to map easily in both. Use dotted names like `llm.model.family` so connectors can translate to tags.

katie: Cardinality policy proposal: model.family and operation are low-card; model.tag allowed but limited to a short set; model.version/build MUST be redacted/normalized before ingestion. If unknown, record `unknown`.

anya: UX for rollouts: when we do canary of a new quantized variant, we want traces grouped by `llm.model.tag` so dashboards can A/B latency & token cost. That implies model.tag must be present on every request.

sam: Also propose `llm.cache.hit` + `llm.cache.policy` and `llm.kv_cache.items` (count) to understand cache effectiveness. Keep cache keys out of spans.

liam: Question: token counts as attributes vs metrics? Metrics are better for long-term agg but traces need per-request counts. Maybe include token counts on span but have pipeline drop or summarize older traces beyond 7d.

katie: TL;DR from me: standard span = `llm.request`; attributes = minimal, low-cardinality model.family + tag; tokens on spans for 7d; token metrics aggregated to long-term store; no prompt content; streaming as events.

anya: I'll push a short RFC with naming examples and retention table. @sam @liam @katie please review. Also adding a small example for pipeline folks to map OTLP to datadog tags.

otel-bot: Note: OTEL exporter compatibility check passed for attribute keys used here (no prohibited characters).

sam: One last thought — include `routing.policy` attribute to link the trace to fallback behavior (e.g., `fallback=true`), helps debug graceful degradation.

anya: Good call. Add `routing.policy` and `routing.fallback` (bool).

katie: I'll prototype dashboards once RFC lands. Need sample queries for p50/p95 latency grouped by `llm.model.tag` & `routing.policy`.

liam: Cool. If we all agree I'll open the PR to telemetry-conventions repo later today.

anya: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
